bpLabel: Fieldstrip Best Practices — this guide follows the Glock-pattern field strip as documented in GLOCK’s own manual, which Grey Ghost Precision’s own page says the Grey Ghost Precision Combat Pistol shares. It is not Grey Ghost Precision’s manual for this model. If you obtain the factory manual, follow it over this guide. Never take this firearm further apart than this guide goes.
cleanIntro:
No manual from Grey Ghost Precision exists for this model, but Grey Ghost Precision’s own page says the Grey Ghost Precision Combat Pistol is built on the Glock pattern, and that pattern’s take-down is documented by GLOCK’s own manual. This guide follows it: clear, prove the pistol empty twice, then the four-component field strip every pistol of the pattern shares. If what you see on yours does not match a step, stop there and clean the pistol locked open instead.

Listed in Fieldstrip as 9mm. The chambering marked on the gun itself is the one that counts — not this guide, and not the listing.

steps.title: Ammunition out of the room, muzzle somewhere safe
steps.action: Before you start, put every loose cartridge, loaded magazine and box of ammunition in another room — a cleaning bench with live rounds on it is where unintended discharges happen. Keep the muzzle pointed where a shot would hurt no one, and keep your finger outside the trigger guard the whole time. Wear eye protection whenever you use solvent or work near a spring, and work where the air moves.
steps.prose: A safety, if yours has one, is never a substitute for an empty chamber, and nothing in this guide relies on one.

steps.title: Confirm yours is built the Glock way
steps.action: Look at the pistol before you touch a control: a flat-faced slide with no external hammer, and on each side of the frame, just above the front of the trigger guard, a small serrated takedown tab (the slide lock). Those tabs are the pattern’s takedown, and this whole guide hangs on them.
steps.prose: ⛔ If yours shows no tabs, a lever instead, or anything you cannot name, this is where the strip ends: clean the pistol locked open and ask Grey Ghost Precision about the rest.

steps.title: Magazine out first — the order is the point
steps.action: Press the magazine catch and take the magazine out of the grip before the slide moves. Working the slide with a magazine in feeds a fresh round into the chamber — that is the classic way an empty pistol stops being empty.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine by pressing the magazine catch
steps.cite: GLOCK Safe Action Pistols — Instructions for Use — EN 09-23 — IX. Field stripping, step 1, p.22

steps.title: Rack it to eject anything in the chamber
steps.action: Hold the grip with your firing hand, finger outside the guard. Grasp the rear of the slide at the serrations and pull it fully back to eject any cartridge in the chamber.
steps.quote: pull the slide fully back to eject any cartridge that may be in the chamber
steps.cite: GLOCK Safe Action Pistols — Instructions for Use — EN 09-23 — IX. Field stripping, step 2, p.22

steps.title: Lock the slide open
steps.action: Push up on the slide stop lever and ease the slide back from fully rearward until it locks open.
steps.quote: Lock the slide in the rearward (open) position by pushing up on the slide stop lever
steps.cite: GLOCK Safe Action Pistols — Instructions for Use — EN 09-23 — IX. Field stripping, step 3, p.22

steps.title: Look AND feel — chamber and magazine well, twice
steps.action: With the slide locked back, look into the chamber and down into the magazine well, then put a fingertip into the chamber: a cartridge that hides in a dark chamber cannot hide from a finger. Close the slide under control, open and lock it again, and check the same way a second time. Both passes, every time — the next step depends on them.
steps.quote: both visually and physically (with your finger) inspect both the chamber and the magazine well of the pistol to be sure that no ammunition remains in either place
steps.cite: GLOCK Safe Action Pistols — Instructions for Use — EN 09-23 — IX. Field stripping, step 4, p.22

steps.title: Slide forward, muzzle safe, then the trigger press the pattern requires
steps.action: Release the slide forward, point the muzzle at something that would stop a bullet, and pull the trigger — you will hear the striker click. On this pattern the striker must be released before the slide will come off; that is GLOCK’s own instruction, not a shortcut. Do this only because you have just proven the chamber and the magazine well empty twice, by eye and by fingertip, in the step above.
steps.quote: With the muzzle of your GLOCK pistol pointed in a safe direction (a safe direction is one in which no one can possibly be injured in the event of an unintentional discharge), pull the trigger.
steps.cite: GLOCK Safe Action Pistols — Instructions for Use — EN 09-23 — IX. Field stripping, step 6, p.22
steps.warn: If the trigger is in the forward position, on your GLOCK pistol may be loaded.

steps.title: Retract about 1/8 inch — no further
steps.action: Using your fingers, draw the slide back about an eighth of an inch and hold it there. Further than that and the trigger resets, and you will be starting over.
steps.quote: Using your fingers, retract the slide (1) about 1/8 in. / 3mm and hold it in this position
steps.cite: GLOCK Safe Action Pistols — Instructions for Use — EN 09-23 — IX. Field stripping, step 8, p.23

steps.title: Both takedown tabs down, evenly
steps.action: With the thumb and index finger of your other hand, pull both serrated tabs of the slide lock down at the same time and hold them.
steps.cite: GLOCK Safe Action Pistols — Instructions for Use — EN 09-23 — IX. Field stripping, step 9, p.23

steps.title: Slide forward off the frame
steps.action: Holding the tabs down, let the slide run forward and off the front of the frame. Set the frame aside — nothing inside it is touched in this guide.
steps.quote: While holding the slide lock down, push the slide forward and off of the frame
steps.cite: GLOCK Safe Action Pistols — Instructions for Use — EN 09-23 — IX. Field stripping, step 10, p.23

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly out
steps.action: Turn the slide over. Press the recoil spring assembly slightly toward the muzzle end, lift it up and out, and set it down the way it sat — it goes back the same way round.
steps.cite: GLOCK Safe Action Pistols — Instructions for Use — EN 09-23 — IX. Field stripping, step 11, p.23

steps.title: Barrel out — four components, and that is the whole strip
steps.action: Hold the barrel by its locking cams, lift it, push it toward the front of the slide, then pull it up and toward the rear to free it. Slide, barrel, recoil spring assembly, frame: that is the complete field strip of the pattern. The striker, the extractor and everything inside the frame stay exactly where they are — work for Grey Ghost Precision.
steps.quote: Holding the barrel by the barrel locking cams, lift it and push it toward the front of the slide and then pull it up and toward the rear to remove it from the slide
steps.cite: GLOCK Safe Action Pistols — Instructions for Use — EN 09-23 — IX. Field stripping, step 12, p.23

steps.title: Bore from the chamber end, breech face wiped
steps.action: With the barrel out, push a brush wet with bore solvent through from the chamber end, a few passes, then dry patches until they come out clean, and a lightly oiled patch for storage. Wipe the breech face and the feed ramp with a cloth and a little solvent; run a dry patch through before you shoot.

steps.title: Rails brushed, then a light film where metal slides
steps.action: Brush the rail cuts in the slide with a nylon brush and a little lubricant, wipe them with a clean patch, and do the same along the frame rails. A drop of oil spread thin on the rails and on the barrel where it rubs the slide is enough; wipe off anything that runs, and keep oil out of the striker channel and the magazine well.
steps.quote: Wet a nylon bristle brush with lubricant and thoroughly brush the rail cuts in the slide
steps.cite: GLOCK Safe Action Pistols — Instructions for Use — EN 09-23 — X. Preventive Maintenance, Clean the slide, step 1, p.29

steps.title: Look for the things that mean stop
steps.action: Hold the barrel up to the light and look through it: you want a clean, unbroken bore with no obstruction, no bulge and no dark ring. Look over the slide, the frame and the barrel for cracks, the recoil spring assembly for kinks or a cracked end, and for anything loose or missing. A screw or pin that has worked loose is reported, not tightened — how tight it should be is a question for Grey Ghost Precision.
steps.prose: Any one of these means the gun is not fired until Grey Ghost Precision has seen it.

deepAbsentReason: There is no deep clean for the Grey Ghost Precision Combat Pistol, and this guide will not invent one. No manual from Grey Ghost Precision exists for this model; the pattern source documents a field strip and nothing deeper for an owner. Anything that needs more than this guide goes to Grey Ghost Precision, not onto the bench.

cleaning.name: BORE
tasks: Brush wet with bore solvent, from the chamber end
Dry patches until clean, then a lightly oiled patch for storage
A dry patch through before the next shot

cleaning.name: BREECH, RAILS & FEED RAMP
tasks: Breech face and feed ramp wiped
Rail cuts brushed and wiped, slide and frame
⛔ No solvent or oil into the striker channel or the frame’s internals

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: A thin film on the rails and where the barrel rubs the slide

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR
tasks: Wiped with a lightly oiled cloth
No solvent on wood, finishes or optics

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: Stored dry — never shut in a closed case while damp
Looked over for rust at every clean

reassembly.title: Barrel into the slide
reassembly.action: Hold the barrel by its locking cams and seat it into the upside-down slide, chamber end to the rear.
reassembly.quote: Holding the barrel (2) by the barrel locking cams, insert it into the slide (1) by pushing it down and in
reassembly.section: XI. Reassembly and inspection, step 1, p.33

reassembly.title: Recoil spring assembly against the barrel
reassembly.action: Small end of the recoil spring assembly into the indentation at the front of the slide, then press the large end down until it rests in the half-moon notch on the barrel’s locking cams.
reassembly.quote: Insert the recoil spring assembly (3) into the slide by placing the small end of the recoil spring assembly in the indentation in the front of the slide
reassembly.section: XI. Reassembly and inspection, step 2, p.33

reassembly.title: Slide onto the frame until the slide lock snaps up
reassembly.action: Finger off the trigger and outside the guard, start the slide onto the frame rails from the front and push it rearward until the slide lock snaps up and holds it.
reassembly.quote: place the slide on top of the frame (17) in front of the slide rails and push the slide towards the back of the frame until the slide lock (21) snaps up to lock the slide into place
reassembly.section: XI. Reassembly and inspection, step 3, p.33

fncheck: Magazine out and the chamber proven empty twice, by eye and fingertip. Rack the slide several times: it should run smooth, with no grit, and lock open on an empty magazine. Then GLOCK’s own inspection, which its manual documents for this pattern: muzzle at a safe backstop, pull the trigger once — a clean click — hold it back, rack the slide, and ease the trigger forward until it resets. If the striker does not click, or the trigger does not reset, the pistol goes to Grey Ghost Precision before it is loaded again.
